claims.text: High configurational entropy produces intrinsic lattice distortions in high-entropy alloys.
Engineered nanoscale interfaces block dislocation motion in HEA multilayer coatings.
The proposed multilayer coating contains alternating layers with controlled lattice mismatch.
The homogeneous comparison film has equivalent composition and lacks engineered multilayer interfaces.
Under the proposed moderate-temperature and strain-rate conditions, dislocation-based plasticity is the dominant deformation mode.
Diffusion effects are minimized under the proposed test conditions.
Lattice-mismatched nanoscale interfaces create coherency strain.
Lattice-mismatched nanoscale interfaces cause dislocation pile-ups.
Intrinsic lattice distortions in the HEA increase the energy barrier for dislocation glide.
Interface blocking and lattice-distortion resistance act together to reduce dislocation mobility.
Reduced dislocation mobility delays time-dependent plastic deformation in multilayer HEA coatings relative to homogeneous films.
Multilayer HEA coatings will exhibit significantly lower creep rates than homogeneous HEA films.
Multilayer HEA coatings will show greater resistance to plastic deformation than homogeneous HEA films.
At extreme temperatures or very high strain rates, additional deformation mechanisms may mask the proposed interface and lattice-distortion effects.
